finding: The new report-target loop walk indexes checked_roles[target] for a role whose own target is undefined. Roles are validated in one pass, so a role earlier in dict order can reach a later role's undefined target and raise KeyError instead of PatternRefused. The CLI does not catch KeyError, so it prints a traceback instead of exit 2.
why: Roles {a: target b, b: target ghost} in that order refuse nothing cleanly, because a's walk reaches 'ghost', appends it to chain, then reads checked_roles['ghost']; the sibling 'reports to ... a role it does not define' check at line 123 only runs when the loop reaches b.
fix: Validate every role's report-target exists in a first pass, then run the self and loop checks in a second pass (or guard the walk with `target in checked_roles`). Add a test with the dangling target on a later role.
evidence: resolver.py:121-130: `for role, fields in checked_roles.items(): target = fields["report-target"]; if target and target not in checked_roles: raise ...` followed by `while target and target not in chain: chain.append(target); target = checked_roles[target]["report-target"]`. The only dangling-target test (test_team_resolver.py:349) uses a single role, so it never walks a chain.

finding: Report-loop test has no pure 3-role ring (a->b->c->a); a mutant detecting only 2-role loops survived all 105 tests.
why: Mutation probe on a copy: replacing the chain walk with a one-hop `report-target == role` check passed the suite, so the general loop walk in _check_record is unproven.
fix: Add {"a": role(target="b"), "b": role(target="c"), "c": role(target="a")} to the parametrize list.
evidence: @pytest.mark.parametrize("roles,needle", [ ({"a": role(target="a")}, ...), ({"a": role(target="b"), "b": role(target="a")}, ...), ({"a": role(target="b"), "b": role(target="c"), "c": role(target="b")}, ...)  (survivor M4: one-hop check)

finding: Moderator part MISSING (no file) is untested; the test writes an empty file only, so the new `if part.is_file() else ""` guard has no test.
why: Mutation probe: reverting _moderator to an unguarded read_text() survived all tests, though the new refusal text says 'missing or empty' and the delta added the guard for the missing case.
fix: Add a case that monkeypatches MODERATOR_PART to a non-existent file name and asserts the same 'charter part is missing or empty' refusal (and that build-verify still resolves).
evidence: part = tmp_path / "moderator.md"; part.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")  (survivor M1: `part.read_text(encoding="utf-8") if part.is_file() else ""` -> `part.read_text(encoding="utf-8")`)

finding: Test named '..._refused_naming_both' cannot tell the colliding role's owner pattern from the debating pattern: both are pattern p, and the assert only checks 'pattern p'.
why: Mutation probe: replacing self.owner[MODERATOR] with the current pattern in the message (and, separately, restricting the check to owner==pattern) survived, so the cross-pattern case where owner and debating pattern differ is unproven.
fix: Define the moderator role in an included saved pattern and the debate step in the includer, then assert both pattern names appear in the message.
evidence: assert "role moderator" in message and "debate step argue" in message and "pattern p" in message  (survivors M2, M8)
